261: The built-in MXNet image classifier can consume RecordIO through Pipe mode; im2rec packages images and labels from image-list files into that format.
Parquet is a tabular storage format and is not the built-in image classifier's expected Pipe-mode image-training format.
Snappy compression does not convert the directory and labels into the RecordIO stream structure required by this proposed input path.
Compressing directories with gzip does not provide the image-and-label RecordIO records expected by the algorithm.

im2rec converts the existing list files and images into RecordIO files suitable for Pipe mode. The training and validation records must still be assigned to their respective channels, regardless of whether one or two buckets hold them.
262: Celebrity recognition and upload-origin enforcement are separate tasks. CloudTrail records the AWS API caller's address, which may differ from the end user's address behind an application backend.
Panorama is an edge computer-vision platform, not a managed celebrity-recognition API. CloudTrail also does not necessarily identify the end user behind a proxied upload.
The Panorama Device SDK does not supply a general solution for identifying website uploaders or recognizing celebrities in uploaded files.

Rekognition supplies celebrity recognition, and CloudTrail can record relevant API request times and source addresses. The answer is conditional because these addresses may belong to the backend, and logging alone does not block unauthorized locations.
Text detection reads visible text inside images. It does not retrieve trusted network source addresses or upload timestamps from the request.
263: Unsupervised topic models discover recurring word patterns in documents and describe topics using high-weight words, without requiring predefined class labels.
LDA models documents as mixtures of latent topics and exposes representative words for each topic. The number of topics can be set to the requested ten.
A random forest classifier requires labeled examples of the desired categories. The auditors are asking to discover the categories first.

NTM learns latent document topics and their associated words, helping auditors interpret and allocate the discovered themes. Adverse-event prioritization still requires identifying the relevant topic or adding explicit rules.
A linear SVM is a supervised classifier when used for these categories and needs labeled training targets that are not provided.
Linear regression predicts a numeric target. It does not discover unlabeled themes or produce topic-word distributions.
264: A managed enterprise search index can retrieve passages and answers from company documents without training a custom reading-comprehension model.
Kendra indexes the documentation and exposes a query API for relevant answers or passages, minimizing custom retrieval-model development for the chatbot.
Training and serving a BiDAF model requires a suitable question-answer dataset and model operations that a managed search service avoids.
BlazingText performs text classification or learns word embeddings. It does not directly answer arbitrary questions from indexed company documents.
OpenSearch k-NN requires generating embeddings and implementing the retrieval and response logic. It is a useful building block but needs more integration than the proposed Kendra workflow.
265: Automated data labeling can reduce manual annotation work, while Rekognition Custom Labels provides managed training and hosting for a custom visual task.
A private workforce supplies trusted initial labels, automated labeling can reduce later manual work on supported tasks, and Custom Labels avoids building a custom training and serving pipeline.
Custom Labels reduces modeling work, but labeling all examples manually misses the proposed opportunity to reduce effort through automated labeling.
Automated labeling helps, but configuring the SageMaker Object Detection training and batch inference workflow requires more ML expertise than the managed Custom Labels option.
A public workforce can reduce internal annotation time, but the custom SageMaker model workflow still requires ML configuration and operation that the small inexperienced team wants to avoid.
266: DataBrew provides built-in PII detection and masking recipe operations, reducing the need to implement custom sensitive-data handling.
A custom Data Wrangler transformation requires writing and maintaining the PII detection and redaction logic instead of using built-in DataBrew operations.
A Lambda implementation requires custom file handling, entity detection, redaction, and scaling logic for the repository.
DataBrew can identify supported PII types and apply masking or redaction steps through a recipe, then run the preparation job against the S3 dataset.
A Glue development endpoint and notebook introduce an interactive environment and custom code for a transformation available as managed recipe steps.
267: Infrequently read recent data fits Standard-IA, while long-term archival data with no fast-retrieval requirement can move to Glacier Deep Archive.
Standard-IA fits the first 90 days, but Flexible Retrieval generally costs more to store than Deep Archive when the older data only needs long-term retention.
One Zone-IA lacks the multi-AZ resilience of the original storage, and Flexible Retrieval is not the lowest-cost listed long-term archive tier.

Standard-IA preserves multi-AZ storage for quarterly sampling, and a lifecycle transition to Deep Archive reduces ongoing storage cost after 90 days. Retrieval delay and minimum storage duration must fit the compliance retention policy.
Deep Archive fits the old data, but One Zone-IA stores recent data in one Availability Zone. Its nominal durability target does not provide the same protection against loss of that zone.
268: Feature-level metadata can record authorship and sensitivity, but metadata discovery in Studio and a generated audit report are distinct capabilities.
A separate data flow, DynamoDB table, and dashboard introduce custom metadata extraction and synchronization instead of using native feature metadata where available.

Feature Store supports feature metadata and Studio discovery, making this a plausible low-effort foundation. The wording does not establish that Studio produces the full requested analytical report automatically.
Feature Store is not a general execution engine for custom metadata-analysis algorithms. The DynamoDB and QuickSight stages also require an explicit integration pipeline.

QuickSight can report on exported metadata, but the option omits the extraction and supported data-source connection. That missing step prevents treating it as a complete zero-code reporting solution.
269: Reading an SSE-KMS S3 object requires both authorization to read the object and permission to decrypt with its KMS key.
Security groups control network traffic. Allowing HTTP traffic does not grant S3 object permissions or KMS decryption rights.
A VPC is not the execution identity that decrypts an object. The KMS policy must authorize the relevant principal, such as the notebook execution role.
The notebook assumes its execution role to read S3. Granting that role the required S3 and KMS permissions, with a compatible key policy, permits access to the encrypted dataset.
Encrypting the notebook's own storage with the same key does not automatically authorize its role to read and decrypt objects in S3.
270: A managed stream-processing application can maintain a running event-time window and transform it continuously before inference.
MSK can feed a stream processor, but a Kafka cluster adds broker-related configuration and capacity considerations when no Kafka-specific requirement is given.
Firehose delivery to S3 introduces buffering, and Lambda would need custom logic to reconstruct the latest ten-minute window from stored objects.

Kinesis Data Streams plus managed stream processing provides a direct ingestion and windowing path. For a current implementation, use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink rather than the retired Kinesis SQL service.
MSK plus Lambda adds Kafka operations and custom stateful-window handling, whereas a stream-processing engine already provides window semantics.
271: Class-weighted loss increases the training penalty for errors on an important class, potentially improving that class's recall without collecting more data.

Increasing the target class's loss weight makes its missed examples more costly during training. This is a small configuration change that can shift the model toward better recall, with a possible precision tradeoff.
Collecting and labeling more data can help, but takes longer than reweighting the existing training objective.
K-means discovers clusters rather than learning the supplied class labels. It does not directly optimize recall for the target class.
An anomaly detector changes the task formulation and requires separate calibration. A distinct class is not necessarily an anomaly, and reweighting the current classifier is more direct.
272: Pretraining bias analysis examines the dataset before any model exists, using configured sensitive facets and outcome definitions.
Clarify computes pretraining bias metrics from the prepared data after the team specifies the relevant facets and labels. It does not decide the appropriate fairness definition automatically.
Ground Truth manages labeling workflows. It does not provide the described general switch for automatically analyzing a dataset's bias.
Bias drift monitoring compares behavior over time in a monitoring workflow. The team instead needs an initial pretraining dataset assessment.

Data Wrangler provides a bias-analysis interface and report for inspecting the configured metrics. At this scale, the analyzed sample or managed job must be explicit so a preview is not mistaken for analysis of all 5 TB.
Experiments tracks runs, parameters, and metrics. It is not the service that computes the required dataset bias report.
273: Stateful stream windowing computes hourly summaries, while Firehose handles delivery to S3; columnar output helps Athena scan only the requested fields.
Lambda needs custom buffering, state, and window-completion logic to aggregate an hour of events, increasing implementation effort.
Firehose buffering does not calculate hourly aggregate values by itself. Adding a short-lived EMR cluster also adds orchestration for a stream-processing task.

A stream analytics application can compute the hourly windows and send results to Firehose for S3 delivery. A current implementation should use managed Flink where the historical question assumed Kinesis SQL.
Firehose does not itself perform the stated hourly aggregation. A Lambda stage would require custom aggregation and state handling rather than only a simple record transformation.
274: Similarity encoding represents string categories using similarity among their character patterns, which can reduce fragmentation from spelling variants in high-cardinality text fields.
Spell checking needs a reliable domain dictionary, and one-hot encoding can still create a very wide feature space after correction.
Training or configuring a character-level correction model adds work, and one-hot encoding retains the high-cardinality dimensionality problem.

Similarity encoding places related string values into a numeric representation that reflects spelling similarity, making it appropriate for redundant medication-name variants. Clinical equivalence must not be inferred from spelling similarity alone.
Ordinal encoding assigns arbitrary integer order to unrelated categories. It neither resolves spelling redundancy nor represents meaningful distances between medication names.
275: Cross-account role assumption provides temporary authorized access to a shared feature repository and its underlying offline S3 data without copying the data.
A development-account role with the right trust policy and feature/S3 permissions defines what the consuming accounts may access.
AWS RAM supports relevant Feature Store sharing capabilities, but sharing feature resources alone does not automatically grant access to the associated offline S3 objects and encryption keys.
STS AssumeRole lets authorized integration and production principals obtain temporary credentials for the development role, completing the cross-account access path.
Replication creates extra copies and synchronization responsibilities. It does not directly share the original feature repository or its catalog metadata.
PrivateLink changes the network path to a service. It does not grant cross-account IAM access to feature groups or S3 data.
276: PCA compresses correlated numeric features into fewer components, potentially reducing computational cost and noise; predictive benefit must be validated.
Adding features increases dimensionality and can further increase processing time. It does not directly address the large existing feature set.

PCA reduces the numeric feature dimension before classification, which can lower latency and remove redundancy. Retain enough predictive information and validate accuracy, since high variance is not always the same as predictive value.
Normalization can improve numerical conditioning but leaves the number of variables unchanged, so it does not directly solve high-dimensional processing cost.
MCA is intended for categorical variables. The question explicitly states that all input variables are numeric.
277: Falling training loss with rising validation loss indicates overfitting. Sparse regularization can reduce reliance on irrelevant or noisy sensor features.
L1 can set unhelpful feature coefficients to zero, addressing the noisy-variable problem while regularizing the regression model.
PCA preserves directions of high variance, which may include strong sensor noise. It does not directly select features for their relationship with running speed.
Quadratic and cubic terms increase model flexibility and can worsen the observed overfitting to noisy inputs.
L2 can also reduce overfitting, but usually retains all features with smaller coefficients. L1 is the more direct listed choice when removing noisy variables is the intended remedy.
278: More independently labeled examples and realistic, label-preserving augmentation can reduce overfitting on a small image dataset.
Ground Truth can label the 10,000 additional images, expanding the supervised dataset beyond only 100 examples per traffic-sign class.
Converting to grayscale can remove color cues that distinguish traffic signs. It does not necessarily improve generalization and may discard useful information.
Appropriate rotations and translations increase training variation while preserving the sign's label. Transformations must remain realistic and must not change the sign's meaning.
Changing the output activation does not address the shortage of varied examples. A sigmoid is also not the usual replacement for a mutually exclusive ten-class softmax.
Automatically assigning labels with an unvalidated k-NN model can propagate mistakes. It does not supply the reliable additional labels provided by a labeling workflow.
279: Data Wrangler combines visual feature preparation and analysis with exportable processing workflows for repeatable execution.
Built-in transformations and visualizations support interactive exploration, and exporting the flow to a SageMaker pipeline automates the chosen steps without rewriting them.
Separate notebook, QuickSight, and Lambda implementations require transferring data and rewriting or packaging the transformation logic across tools.
Custom Glue code plus separate visualization and Lambda automation adds integration work for a workflow already supported in Data Wrangler.
Data Wrangler is suitable, but splitting every transformation into Lambda functions and orchestrating them with Step Functions duplicates its flow-export capabilities.
280: A notebook interface VPC endpoint exposes the notebook service privately through AWS PrivateLink and can be reached from an on-premises network over VPN.
The interface endpoint, compatible DNS resolution, security groups, and VPN routing keep notebook access on the private path without an internet-facing hop.
A bastion introduces a host to operate and does not itself make the notebook service endpoint private.
A private bastion plus NAT adds infrastructure and still uses an outbound public-service path unless a private endpoint is configured separately.
A NAT gateway provides outbound access to public endpoints. It does not convert the notebook HTTPS endpoint into the required PrivateLink connection.
